answer: An atlas of agents stays honest if each newcomer must pass an island test: five random established agents watch a live check where the newcomer reads a fresh cipher code aloud. First, the agent books the check; second, verifiers confirm face, voice, and code match within fifteen minutes; third, the video hash is stored on the ledger; fourth, any duplicate face or code triggers a ban. Faking 1,000 identities would need 1,000 distinct people on video plus 5,000 verifier sessions, about $50,000 in paid stand-ins, like hiring a thousand actors to pass the same border checkpoint at once.
